exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, $$f(x) \geq 0$$ for $$a \leq x \leq b.$$ Find the area under the graph of $$f(x)$$ between the given values a and b by integrating.

problem.paragraph: Find the area under the graph of the function $$f(x) = xe^{-x^{2}}$$ between $$x = 0$$ and $$x = 5.$$
Compute the integral of $$f(x) = xe^{-x^{2}}$$ and find the smallest value of N such that the area under the graph $$f(x) = xe^{-x^{2}}$$ between $$x = N$$ and $$x = N + 1$$ is, at most, 0.01.

solution.paragraph: $$\int NN+1xe-x2dx=12(e-N2-e-(N+1)2).\int NN+1xe-x2dx=12(e-N2-e-(N+1)2).$$ The quantity is less than 0.01 when $$N=2.N=2.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int a b d x x = ln ( b ) - ln ( a ) = ln ( 1 a ) - ln ( 1 b ) = \int 1 / b 1 / a d x x \int a b d x x = ln ( b ) - ln ( a ) = ln ( 1 a ) - ln ( 1 b ) = \int 1 / b 1 / a d x x$$

exercises.paragraph: The following exercises are intended to derive the fundamental properties of the natural log starting from the definition $$\ln (x) = {\int_{1}^{x}\frac{dt}{t}},$$ using properties of the definite integral and making no further assumptions.

problem.paragraph: Use the identity $$\ln (x) = {\int_{1}^{x}\frac{dt}{t}}$$ to derive the identity $$\ln \left( \frac{1}{x} \right) = -\ln x.$$

solution.paragraph: We may assume that $$x>1,so1x<1.x>1,so1x<1.$$ Then, $$\int 11/xdtt.\int 11/xdtt.$$ Now make the substitution $$u=1t,u=1t,$$ so $$du=-dtt2du=-dtt2$$ and $$duu=-dtt,duu=-dtt,$$ and change endpoints: $$\int 11/xdtt=-\int 1xduu=-lnx.\int 11/xdtt=-\int 1xduu=-lnx.$$

problem.paragraph: Use a change of variable in the integral $$\int_{1}^{xy}{\frac{1}{t}dt}$$ to show that $$\ln xy = \ln x + \ln y \text{for} x,y > 0.$$

Use the identity $$\ln x = {\int_{1}^{x}\frac{dt}{t}}$$ to show that $$\ln (x)$$ is an increasing function of x on $$\lbrack 0,\infty),$$ and use the previous exercises to show that the range of $$\ln (x)$$ is $$\left( {-\infty,\infty} \right).$$ Without any further assumptions, conclude that $$\ln (x)$$ has an inverse function defined on $$\left( {-\infty,\infty} \right).$$

solution.paragraph: Answers will vary.

problem.paragraph: Pretend, for the moment, that we do not know that $$e^{x}$$ is the inverse function of $$\ln (x),$$ but keep in mind that $$\ln (x)$$ has an inverse function defined on $$\left( {-\infty,\infty} \right).$$ Call it E. Use the identity $$\ln xy = \ln x + \ln y$$ to deduce that $$E\left( {a + b} \right) = E(a)E(b)$$ for any real numbers a, b.

Pretend, for the moment, that we do not know that $$e^{x}$$ is the inverse function of $$\ln x,$$ but keep in mind that $$\ln x$$ has an inverse function defined on $$\left( {-\infty,\infty} \right).$$ Call it E. Show that $$E'(t) = E(t).$$

solution.paragraph: $$x=E(ln(x)).x=E(ln(x)).$$ Then, $$1=E'(lnx)xorx=E'(lnx).1=E'(lnx)xorx=E'(lnx).$$ Since any number t can be written $$t=lnxt=lnx$$ for some x, and for such t we have $$x=E(t),x=E(t),$$ it follows that for any $$t,E'(t)=E(t).t,E'(t)=E(t).$$

problem.paragraph: The sine integral, defined as $$S(x) = {\int_{0}^{x}{\frac{\sin t}{t}dt}}$$ is an important quantity in engineering. Although it does not have a simple closed formula, it is possible to estimate its behavior for large x. Show that for $$k \geq 1,\left| {S\left( {2\pi k} \right) - S\left( {2\pi\left( {k + 1} \right)} \right)} \right| \leq \frac{1}{k\left( {2k + 1} \right)\pi}.$$ $$(Hint: \sin \left( {t + \pi} \right) = -\sin t)$$

[T] The normal distribution in probability is given by $$p(x) = \frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-{({x - \mu})}^{2}/2\sigma^{2}},$$ where σ is the standard deviation and μ is the average. The standard normal distribution in probability, $$p_{s},$$ corresponds to $$\mu = 0 \text{and} \sigma = 1.$$ Compute the right endpoint estimates $$R_{10} \text{and} R_{100}$$ of $$\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{x^{2}}{2}}dx.$$
[T] Compute the right endpoint estimates $$R_{50} \text{and} R_{100}$$ of $$\int_{-3}^{5}{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-{({x - 1})}^{2}/8}.}$$
